question: An LLC owned by one individual files no Form 8832. For federal income tax it is:
explanation: Under Reg. 301.7701-3(b)(1), a domestic eligible entity with a single owner is disregarded by default, so an individual owner reports the business on Schedule C. A partnership needs at least two members.

question: A domestic LLC with three members never files Form 8832. Its default classification is:
explanation: Reg. 301.7701-3(b)(1) classifies a domestic eligible entity with two or more members as a partnership unless it elects otherwise. S status needs a corporation, or an entity electing to be one, plus Form 2553.

question: The effective date chosen on Form 8832 can be no earlier than how many days before the election is filed?
explanation: Reg. 301.7701-3(c)(1)(iii) lets an entity classification election take effect no more than 75 days before, and no more than 12 months after, the date Form 8832 is filed. Rev. Proc. 2009-41 offers late election relief.

question: Spouses who own an unincorporated business together, file jointly and elect qualified joint venture status report its income:
optionD: On a Schedule C for each
explanation: A qualified joint venture election under section 761(f) lets each spouse report a share of income and expense on a separate Schedule C and Schedule SE instead of filing a partnership return.

question: The qualified joint venture election is not available when the spouses run the business through:
optionD: A business that has a loss
explanation: A qualified joint venture covers a business the spouses own directly. A business held in a state-law entity such as an LLC files as a partnership, or the couple may in a community property state treat it under Rev. Proc. 2002-69.

question: Which sole proprietor must get an employer identification number?
optionA: One who files a Schedule C
explanation: A sole proprietor needs an EIN to pay wages, file excise or pension plan returns, or in a few other cases. A proprietor with no employees may use a Social Security number on Schedule C and Schedule SE.

question: A sole proprietor takes in a partner and the business now operates as a partnership. Its EIN:
explanation: A partnership is a new taxpayer, so it needs its own EIN, applied for on Form SS-4 or online. The proprietor's old number belonged to the proprietorship.

question: A newly formed C corporation that is not a personal service corporation may adopt for its first return:
explanation: A new C corporation adopts its tax year by filing its first return on that basis, and may pick a calendar or any fiscal year. Partnerships, S corporations and personal service corporations face required-year rules instead.

question: When partners holding a majority interest share the same tax year, the partnership must generally use:
optionB: A calendar year in all cases
optionD: Any year the partners agree to
explanation: Section 706(b) applies the majority-interest year first, then the year of all principal partners, then the year giving the least aggregate deferral. A business purpose or a section 444 election can allow another year.

question: A partnership wants a fiscal year other than its required year without showing a business purpose. It may make a:
explanation: Section 444, made on Form 8716, lets a partnership, S corporation or personal service corporation keep a limited deferral period, with required payments under section 7519 for partnerships and S corporations.

question: For 2025 wages, an employer must file Form W-2 Copy A with the Social Security Administration by:
explanation: Copy A of Form W-2 and Form W-3 are due to the SSA by January 31, the same day employees must receive their copies. The older paper and electronic deadlines in late February and March no longer apply to W-2s.

question: A new employee never gives the employer a Form W-4. The employer withholds income tax as if the employee were:
explanation: Publication 15 tells employers to withhold as for a single or married filing separately employee with no other entries in Steps 2, 3 and 4 when no valid Form W-4 is furnished.

question: A business paid an unincorporated contractor $5,000 for repair services in 2025. It reports the payment on:
explanation: Payments of $600 or more for services by a nonemployee are nonemployee compensation on Form 1099-NEC. Form 1099-MISC still covers items such as rents and royalties, and Form 1099-K is filed by payment settlement entities.

question: An activity other than horse breeding is presumed to be engaged in for profit if it shows a profit in:
explanation: Section 183(d) presumes a profit motive if gross income exceeds deductions in 3 of 5 consecutive years. The 2 of 7 years test applies only to breeding, training, showing or racing horses.

question: A taxpayer who wants to delay the IRS's decision on whether a new activity is a hobby files:
explanation: Form 5213 elects to postpone the profit-motive determination until the end of the fifth year (seventh for horses), and it extends the assessment period for that activity. Forms 8832, 1128 and 3115 deal with classification, tax years and methods.

question: A homeowners association that elects to be taxed under section 528 files:
explanation: A qualifying homeowners association may elect each year on Form 1120-H to exclude exempt function income such as member dues and pay tax only on other net income. Without the election it files Form 1120.

question: A partnership pays commissions to a broker to sell interests to new investors. Under section 709 these syndication costs are:
explanation: Section 709(a) denies any deduction for amounts paid to promote or sell partnership interests, and the 709(b) election to deduct and amortize covers only organizational expenses, not syndication costs.

question: A limited partner who performs no services receives only a distributive share of ordinary income. For self-employment tax, that share is:
explanation: Section 1402(a)(13) excludes a limited partner's distributive share from net earnings from self-employment. Only guaranteed payments for services actually rendered are included for a limited partner.

question: A guaranteed payment a calendar-year partner receives from a fiscal-year partnership is included in the partner's income:
optionA: When the cash is actually received
optionB: When the payment agreement is signed
optionC: For the year the partnership year ends
explanation: Section 706(a) bases a partner's inclusions under sections 702 and 707(c) on the partnership year ending within or with the partner's year, so a guaranteed payment is reported with that year's K-1, not when paid.

question: A 70% partner sells equipment to the partnership at a gain, and the partnership will depreciate it in its business. The partner's gain is:
explanation: Section 707(b)(2) makes gain ordinary on a sale between a partnership and a more-than-50% partner of property that is not a capital asset in the buyer's hands, such as depreciable business equipment.

question: A domestic partnership must file Form 1065 for any tax year in which it:
explanation: The Form 1065 instructions require a return from every domestic partnership unless it neither receives income nor incurs expenditures treated as deductions or credits. A loss year still needs a return.

question: An eligible partnership elects out of the centralized audit regime by:
optionB: Filing Schedule B-2 with a timely return
explanation: Section 6221(b) requires the election on a timely filed return for that year, made on Schedule B-2 (Form 1065) with each partner's name and TIN, and the partners must be notified within 30 days.

question: Form 7004 gives a partnership an automatic extension to file Form 1065 of:
explanation: A timely Form 7004 extends a partnership's filing deadline by 6 months, to the 15th day of the 9th month for a calendar-year partnership. It does not extend time for partners to report their own taxes.

question: The penalty for filing Form 1065 late without reasonable cause is figured for:
optionA: Each month on the unpaid tax
optionC: The return as one flat amount
optionD: Each partner for each month late
explanation: Section 6698 imposes a penalty per month or part of a month, up to 12 months, multiplied by the number of persons who were partners at any time during the year. A partnership owes no income tax to base it on.

question: Each partner must receive a Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) by:
explanation: Section 6031(b) requires the partnership to furnish each partner's K-1 on or before the day the return is required to be filed, including extensions.

question: Under the centralized partnership audit regime, the person with sole authority to act for the partnership is the:
explanation: Section 6223 requires a partnership representative, who binds the partnership and all partners in the audit. The tax matters partner belonged to the TEFRA rules that ended for years after 2017.

question: A partnership representative under section 6223 must:
optionB: Be a CPA or enrolled agent
explanation: Section 6223 allows a partner or other person with a substantial presence in the United States to be the partnership representative. That person need not be a partner or a licensed practitioner.

question: A partnership may elect out of the centralized audit regime for 2025 only if it has:
optionA: 100 or fewer partners of any kind
explanation: An eligible partnership has 100 or fewer partners, all individuals, C corporations, S corporations (counting their shareholders), eligible foreign entities or estates of deceased partners. The election is made each year on Schedule B-2.

question: A partnership has eight partners, one of which is another partnership. For the centralized audit regime it:
optionB: May elect out on Schedule B-2
optionC: May elect out with partner consent
optionD: Is out by default under 10 partners
explanation: A partnership is not an eligible partner, so a partnership with a partnership as a partner cannot elect out under section 6221(b), however few partners it has. The old small partnership exception no longer applies.

question: Under the centralized audit regime, an imputed underpayment is generally paid by:
explanation: Section 6225 assesses the imputed underpayment against the partnership in the adjustment year. Partners bear it only through the partnership, unless the partnership elects to push the adjustments out.

question: To push audit adjustments out to its reviewed-year partners, a partnership must elect within:
explanation: Section 6226 requires the push-out election no later than 45 days after the date of the notice of final partnership adjustment. The reviewed-year partners then take the adjustments into account.

question: A partnership's insolvency exclusion for canceled debt income is tested:
explanation: Section 108(d)(6) applies the bankruptcy, insolvency and similar exclusions at the partner level. A partner who is solvent includes the share of canceled debt even if the partnership itself is insolvent.

question: Ava sells her partnership interest for $30,000 cash, and the buyer takes over her $12,000 share of partnership liabilities. Her amount realized is:
explanation: Relief from a share of partnership liabilities is treated as money received under section 752(d), so the amount realized is $30,000 + $12,000 = $42,000.

question: Payments to a retiring partner for her share of partnership property are treated under section 736(b) as:
explanation: Section 736(b) treats liquidating payments made for a retiring or deceased partner's interest in partnership property as distributions. Other payments are a distributive share or guaranteed payments under section 736(a).

question: For section 751, a partnership's unrealized receivables include its:
explanation: Section 751(c) treats depreciation recapture the partnership would have on a sale of its assets as an unrealized receivable, alongside rights to payment for goods and services not yet included in income.

question: Under section 708, a partnership terminates for tax purposes when:
optionA: Half its interests sell in 12 months
optionD: No partner carries on any business
explanation: After 2017 a partnership ends only when no part of its business continues to be carried on by any partner in a partnership. The old technical termination on a 50% sale was repealed by the 2017 tax act.

question: When a partner dies, the partnership's tax year:
explanation: Section 706(c)(2)(A) closes the year for a partner whose entire interest terminates, by death or otherwise, so the decedent's share up to the date of death goes on the final individual return.

question: A partner contributes a capital asset she held 3 years for a partnership interest. Her holding period for the interest:
explanation: Under section 1223(1), a partnership interest received for a capital or section 1231 asset in a nontaxable exchange takes the holding period of the property contributed.

question: Partnership capital accounts on 2025 Schedules K-1 must be reported using:
explanation: The Form 1065 instructions require item L capital accounts to be reported on the tax basis method. A partner's tax capital account can still differ from adjusted basis, which also counts liabilities.

question: Once a partnership makes a section 754 election, it applies:
optionA: Only to the year it is made
optionB: Only to the sale that prompted it
explanation: A section 754 election covers the year made and all later years, so basis adjustments under sections 734(b) and 743(b) apply to every later distribution and transfer until the IRS consents to revocation.

question: For tax years beginning in 2025, a C corporation's regular income tax rate is:
explanation: Section 11(b) has taxed all C corporation taxable income at a flat 21% since 2018. The graduated 15% to 35% brackets ended with the 2017 tax act.

question: A corporation owns 85% of another domestic corporation in its affiliated group. Its deduction for qualifying dividends from that member is:
explanation: Section 243(a)(3) and (b) allow a 100% deduction for qualifying dividends from a member of the same affiliated group, which needs 80% ownership. Lower ownership gets 65% or 50%.

question: For 2025, a C corporation's charitable contribution deduction is generally limited to what share of taxable income, figured before the deduction?
explanation: Section 170(b)(2) caps a corporation's deduction at 10% of taxable income figured without the charitable deduction, the dividends received deduction and carrybacks. The 1% floor added by the 2025 law starts in 2026.

question: A corporation's charitable contributions above the annual limit may be carried forward for:
explanation: Section 170(d)(2) carries a corporation's excess contributions forward to the 5 succeeding tax years, used after that year's own contributions. There is no carryback.

question: A C corporation has a 2025 net capital loss. It may:
optionA: Carry it back 3 and forward 5 years
optionD: Deduct it fully against ordinary income
explanation: Section 1211(a) lets a corporation deduct capital losses only against capital gains, and section 1212(a) carries a net capital loss back 3 years and forward 5 as a short-term loss. The $3,000 allowance is for individuals.

question: A net capital loss a C corporation carries back to an earlier year is treated there as a:
explanation: Section 1212(a)(1) treats a corporation's capital loss carryback or carryover as a short-term capital loss in each year it is carried to, usable only against capital gains.

question: Before a redemption Ann owned 60% of a corporation's voting stock; after it she owns 45%. Under section 302(b)(2) the redemption:
optionD: Qualifies for any drop in shares
explanation: A substantially disproportionate redemption leaves the shareholder with less than 50% of the voting stock and less than 80% of her prior percentage. 80% of 60% is 48%, and 45% is below both lines, so it is a sale, not a dividend.

question: To waive family attribution in a complete redemption, the former shareholder must not acquire an interest, other than by inheritance, for:
explanation: Section 302(c)(2) waives family attribution only if the distributee keeps no interest other than as a creditor, acquires none (except by bequest or inheritance) within 10 years, and files the required agreement.

question: The accumulated earnings credit lets most C corporations accumulate, as reasonable needs, at least:
explanation: Section 535(c)(2) gives a minimum credit of $250,000 less accumulated E&P at the start of the year. Personal service corporations in fields such as health, law and accounting get $150,000.

question: The accumulated earnings tax is imposed on accumulated taxable income at a rate of:
explanation: Section 531 imposes the accumulated earnings tax at 20% of accumulated taxable income, in addition to regular tax. The rate rose from 15% in 2013.

question: A calendar-year corporation's 2025 estimated tax installments are due on the 15th day of the:
explanation: Section 6655(c) sets corporate installments for April 15, June 15, September 15 and December 15 for a calendar year. The January installment pattern belongs to individuals.

question: A corporation owes no penalty for underpaying 2025 estimated tax if the tax shown on its return is less than:
explanation: Section 6655(f) exempts a corporation from the addition to tax when the tax shown on the return is less than $500. Individuals use a $1,000 threshold under section 6654.

question: A corporation files Form 7004 for its 2025 Form 1120. The extension:
explanation: Form 7004 gives an automatic 6-month extension to file. The tax is still due by the original due date, and interest and the late-payment penalty run on any unpaid balance.

question: To figure current earnings and profits from taxable income, a corporation adds back:
explanation: E&P reflects economic income, so tax-exempt interest is added. Federal income taxes, excess charitable gifts and nondeductible premiums are subtracted, because they reduce the cash available to pay dividends.

question: For section 351 to apply, the transferors of property as a group must own, right after the exchange, at least:
optionA: 50% of vote and of other shares
optionB: 80% of vote or of total value
optionC: 80% of vote and of other shares
explanation: Section 368(c) defines control as 80% of total combined voting power and 80% of the shares of each other class. The 80% vote or value test belongs to the controlled group rules.

question: A parent-subsidiary controlled group exists when the parent owns, of the subsidiary's stock, at least:
explanation: Section 1563(a)(1) needs stock with at least 80% of total voting power or at least 80% of total value. The 351 control test, by contrast, requires vote and each other class.

question: For the controlled group limits, a brother-sister group exists when five or fewer individuals own, counting identical holdings in each corporation:
explanation: For the section 1561 limits, a brother-sister group is tested only on more than 50% identical ownership by five or fewer individuals, estates or trusts, measured in each corporation by vote or value.

question: Members of a controlled group of corporations must share:
explanation: Section 1561 divides items such as the accumulated earnings credit among group members. The graduated brackets it once divided ended in 2018, and each member keeps its own EIN unless it joins a consolidated return.

question: A closely held C corporation, not a personal service corporation, may use its passive activity losses to offset:
explanation: Section 469(e)(2) lets a closely held C corporation deduct passive losses against net active income, but not against portfolio income such as interest and dividends.

question: A calendar-year accrual corporation's board authorized a charitable gift in December 2025. To deduct it for 2025, the corporation must pay it by:
explanation: Section 170(a)(2) lets an accrual corporation elect to treat a board-authorized gift as paid in 2025 if paid by the 15th day of the 4th month after year end, April 15, 2026.

question: An S election may be revoked with the consent of shareholders holding:
optionA: More than half of the shares
explanation: Section 1362(d)(1) allows revocation with consent of shareholders holding more than one-half of the outstanding shares, voting and nonvoting, on the day the revocation is made.

question: A calendar-year S corporation takes on a partnership as a shareholder on June 30, 2025. For 2025 it files:
optionA: One S return for the full year
optionB: An S short year and a C short year
optionC: One C return for the full year
explanation: Section 1362(e) splits the termination year into an S short year ending the day before termination and a C short year starting that day, generally allocating income pro rata by days.

question: Eli's S stock basis is $4,000 at the start of 2025. His shares are $5,000 of income and a $6,000 loss, and he receives an $8,000 distribution. How much of the loss can he deduct?
explanation: Basis rises for income to $9,000, then falls for the distribution to $1,000, and only then for losses, so $1,000 of the loss is allowed and $5,000 is suspended. Taking the loss before the distribution gives $6,000, the wrong order.

question: Health insurance an S corporation pays for a more-than-2% shareholder-employee is:
optionD: Included in the owner's W-2 wages
explanation: A more-than-2% shareholder is treated as a partner for fringe benefits, so the premiums are deductible by the corporation and included in Form W-2 box 1 wages. The shareholder may then take the self-employed health insurance deduction.

question: An insolvent S corporation has debt canceled in 2025. The insolvency exclusion is applied:
explanation: Section 108(d)(7) applies the exclusions at the corporate level for an S corporation, and excluded income does not increase shareholders' basis. Partnerships, by contrast, test insolvency partner by partner.

question: Which item does an S corporation report separately on Schedule K-1 rather than in ordinary business income?
explanation: The section 179 dollar and income limits apply at both the corporation and the shareholder level, so the deduction passes through separately. Salaries, rent and repairs are netted in ordinary business income.

question: A corporation missed the deadline for its S election. Late election relief under Rev. Proc. 2013-30 is generally requested within:
explanation: The Form 2553 instructions allow late election relief if requested within 3 years and 75 days of the intended effective date, with reasonable cause shown. Two months and 15 days is the normal deadline.

question: An S corporation with no business purpose for another year and no section 444 election must use:
explanation: Section 1378 requires an S corporation to use a permitted year, the calendar year, unless it shows a business purpose or elects a fiscal year under section 444.

question: Losses suspended for lack of basis when an S election terminates may be deducted:
explanation: Section 1366(d)(3) treats suspended losses as incurred on the last day of the post-termination transition period, to the extent of the shareholder's stock basis at that time.

question: An S corporation treats its wholly owned subsidiary as a qualified subchapter S subsidiary by filing:
explanation: Form 8869 makes the QSub election, so the subsidiary's assets and income are treated as the parent's. Form 2553 elects S status, Form 8832 classifies eligible entities, and Form 966 reports a dissolution.

question: An S corporation's accumulated adjustments account can fall below zero because of:
explanation: Section 1368(e)(1) adjusts AAA like stock basis but disregards the not-below-zero rule for losses. Distributions cannot push AAA below zero, and tax-exempt income does not change it.

question: Which trust can hold stock in an S corporation?
explanation: Section 1361 lets a qualified subchapter S trust, an electing small business trust, a grantor trust and certain others hold S stock. Foreign trusts, charitable remainder trusts and IRAs are not permitted shareholders.

question: In 2025 an accrual business with no applicable financial statement receives payment for services it will perform in 2025 and 2026. It may:
optionC: Defer it over the service term
explanation: Section 451(c) allows a one-year deferral of the part of an advance payment not earned by the end of the year of receipt. The deferred part must be included in the next year, however long the service runs.

question: Which cost does a retailer include in cost of goods sold?
explanation: Cost of goods sold includes the purchase price and the cost of getting goods to the business, such as freight-in. Delivery to customers, advertising and sales commissions are selling expenses.

question: For 2025, a reseller is exempt from the uniform capitalization rules if it:
explanation: Section 263A(i) exempts a small business taxpayer, one meeting the section 448(c) gross receipts test, from UNICAP. Method of accounting, staff size and sales channel do not matter.

question: A business that first adopts the LIFO inventory method files:
explanation: Form 970 is the application to use LIFO, attached to the return for the first year it is used. Form 3115 is for most other method changes, including changing out of LIFO.

question: For the at-risk rules, which amount counts as at risk in a business activity?
optionD: Loans from someone with an interest
explanation: Section 465 treats as at risk cash and property contributed and amounts borrowed for which the taxpayer is personally liable. Nonrecourse debt, protected amounts and loans from interested persons generally are not.

question: A solvent sole proprietor, not in bankruptcy, has a vendor forgive $8,000 she owed for repair services she had deducted. The $8,000 is:
explanation: Canceled business debt is income under section 61(a)(11) unless an exclusion applies. A solvent taxpayer outside bankruptcy whose debt is not qualified real property or farm debt has no exclusion, and the purchase price reduction rule covers only debt for property bought, not services.

question: A sole proprietor gives $1,000 of business funds to a public charity. The gift is deducted:
optionA: On Schedule C as an expense
optionB: On Schedule SE as an offset
explanation: A sole proprietorship's charitable gift is a personal deduction of the owner, taken on Schedule A when itemizing. It is not a Schedule C business expense and does not reduce self-employment income.

question: An accrual corporation accrues a 2025 bonus for an employee who owns no stock. The bonus is deductible for 2025 if paid by:
explanation: Compensation paid within 2 1/2 months after year end is not treated as deferred compensation, so an accrual business deducts it in the year accrued if paid by March 15. Later payment moves the deduction to the year paid.

question: An accrual corporation accrues salary to its 70% cash-basis shareholder in December 2025 and pays it in February 2026. The corporation deducts it:
explanation: Section 267(a)(2) defers an accrual payer's deduction to a related cash-method payee until the payee includes the amount in income. A more-than-50% owner is related, so the 2 1/2 month rule does not help.

question: Which benefit can an employer exclude from wages as a de minimis fringe?
optionA: Gift cards of a small value
optionB: Occasional snacks in the break room
explanation: A de minimis fringe is property or a service so small and infrequent that accounting for it is unreasonable. Cash and cash equivalents such as gift cards are never de minimis, whatever the amount.

question: Ben, 16, works for his father's sole proprietorship. His wages are:
explanation: Section 3121(b)(3) excludes a child under 18 employed by a parent's sole proprietorship from FICA, and section 3306(c)(5) excludes a child under 21 from FUTA. The wages are still subject to income tax.

question: Kim works as an employee of her husband's sole proprietorship. Her wages are subject to:
explanation: A spouse employed by the other spouse's business is covered for Social Security and Medicare, but section 3306(c)(5) excludes the spouse's services from federal unemployment tax.

question: A statutory employee, with box 13 checked on Form W-2, reports the wages and expenses on:
explanation: Statutory employees deduct business expenses on Schedule C, but the employer already withheld Social Security and Medicare, so no self-employment tax is figured on that income.

question: Lena rents a building she owns to a business in which she materially participates. Her net rental income is:
explanation: Under the self-rental rule in Reg. 1.469-2(f)(6), net rental income from property rented to a business in which the owner materially participates is recharacterized as nonpassive, so it cannot absorb passive losses.

question: A cash-method business prepays 18 months of office rent on July 1, 2025. Its 2025 deduction covers:
explanation: The 12-month rule allows a current deduction only if the benefit ends by the earlier of 12 months after it begins or the end of the next year. An 18-month benefit fails, so rent is deducted as it applies: July to December 2025.

question: Unlike a nonbusiness bad debt, a business bad debt is deductible:
explanation: Section 166(a)(2) allows a business bad debt deduction for the part charged off when the debt becomes partly worthless, as an ordinary loss. A nonbusiness bad debt must be totally worthless and is a short-term capital loss.

question: A cash-method consultant cannot collect a $4,000 fee she billed in 2025. Her bad debt deduction is:
explanation: A cash-method taxpayer never included the fee in income, so it has no basis in the receivable and nothing to deduct. Only amounts previously included in income can become a deductible bad debt.

question: A self-employed taxpayer pays $240 for a business meal with a client in 2025. The deductible amount is:
explanation: Section 274(n) limits business meals to 50% of cost, here $120. The 80% rate applies only to meals of workers under Department of Transportation hours-of-service limits.

question: A business buys baseball tickets, with no food, for a client in 2025. The cost is:
explanation: Since 2018 section 274(a) disallows entertainment, amusement or recreation expenses even when business is discussed. Food bought separately may still qualify for the 50% meal deduction.

question: A business gives a client a $60 gift basket in 2025, its only gift to her this year. The deduction is:
explanation: Section 274(b) limits the deduction for business gifts to $25 per recipient per year. Incidental costs such as engraving or shipping do not count toward the $25.

question: To use the standard mileage rate for a car the business owns, the taxpayer must:
optionA: Choose it in the car's first year
optionB: Choose it in any later year
optionC: Own five or more cars at once
optionD: Claim MACRS in the first year
explanation: The standard mileage rate for an owned car must be chosen in the first year the car is used for business. It cannot be used after MACRS was claimed or for five or more cars used at the same time.

question: For tax purposes, interest on a loan is classified as business, investment or personal by:
optionB: How the loan proceeds are used
optionC: Who the lender of the money is
optionD: How long the loan's term runs
explanation: Under the interest tracing rules of Temp. Reg. 1.163-8T, interest is allocated by the use of the borrowed money, not by the collateral. A home equity loan spent on equipment yields business interest.

question: A business is exempt from the section 163(j) business interest limit for 2025 if it:
optionA: Has no foreign owners at all
optionB: Uses the cash method for all items
explanation: Section 163(j)(3) exempts a small business that meets the section 448(c) gross receipts test, other than a tax shelter. For others, business interest is limited to 30% of adjusted taxable income plus interest income.

question: A self-employed person may take the self-employed health insurance deduction for any month in which she:
optionA: Has a net loss from her business
optionD: Is not eligible for an employer plan
explanation: Section 162(l) denies the deduction for months the person is eligible for a subsidized plan through an employer or a spouse's employer, and limits it to earned income from the business.

question: A sole proprietor buys overhead insurance that pays the business's rent and utilities if she is disabled for a long period. The premiums are:
optionD: Deductible only by a C corporation
explanation: Publication 334 lists overhead insurance covering business overhead during long disability as a deductible insurance expense. Premiums for disability insurance replacing her own lost income are personal.

question: An employer's FUTA tax paid for its employees is:
explanation: The employer's share of FICA and its FUTA tax are deductible taxes of the business. FUTA is paid only by the employer, never withheld from wages.

question: A business deducted $2,000 of a state tax in 2024 and receives a refund of it in 2025. The refund is:
explanation: Under the tax benefit rule of section 111, a recovery of an amount deducted in an earlier year is income in the year recovered, to the extent the deduction reduced tax. The earlier return is not amended.

question: Which business is a specified service trade or business for the qualified business income deduction?
explanation: Section 199A(d)(2) uses the section 1202(e)(3)(A) list but drops engineering and architecture, so those are not SSTBs. Consulting remains on the list, which limits the deduction above the income threshold.

question: Above the threshold, a non-SSTB's QBI deduction is limited to the greater of 50% of W-2 wages or:
explanation: Section 199A(b)(2)(B) caps the deduction for each business at the greater of 50% of W-2 wages or 25% of W-2 wages plus 2.5% of the unadjusted basis immediately after acquisition of qualified property.

question: Besides businesses with gross receipts of $1 million or less, the disabled access credit is open to businesses that last year had:
explanation: Section 44(b) defines an eligible small business by gross receipts of $1 million or less or no more than 30 full-time employees in the prior year, counting those working 30 hours or more a week for 20 weeks.

question: To claim the small business health care tax credit, an employer must have:
explanation: Section 45R limits the credit to employers with fewer than 25 full-time equivalent employees and average wages under an indexed limit, paying at least half of premiums for coverage bought through a SHOP Marketplace.

question: The farming loss portion of a 2025 net operating loss may be:
explanation: Section 172(b)(1)(B) keeps a 2-year carryback for farming losses, which the taxpayer may waive. Other losses arising after 2020 are carried forward only.

question: A noncorporate taxpayer's excess business loss disallowed for 2025 is:
explanation: Section 461(l)(2) treats an excess business loss disallowed in a year as part of the net operating loss carried to later years, where it is subject to the NOL rules.

question: To deduct a home office as a principal place of business, the space must be used:
explanation: Section 280A(c)(1) requires regular and exclusive use for the business, apart from the day care and inventory storage exceptions. Occasional use or mixed personal use fails.

question: Under the simplified method for a home office, the deduction is:
optionA: $5 a square foot, up to 250 sq ft
optionB: $3 a square foot, up to 300 sq ft
optionC: $5 a square foot, up to 300 sq ft
optionD: $5 a square foot, with no cap
explanation: Rev. Proc. 2013-13 sets a prescribed rate of $5 per square foot for up to 300 square feet, so at most $1,500, still limited to the business's gross income from the use. No home depreciation is taken that year.

question: Business equipment with an adjusted basis of $9,000 and a value of $6,000 is totally destroyed by fire with no insurance. The deductible loss is:
explanation: For business property completely destroyed, the loss is the adjusted basis, less any insurance, under Reg. 1.165-7(b). The $100 reduction and 10% of AGI rules apply only to personal-use property.

question: Qualified property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025 is eligible for a special depreciation allowance of:
explanation: Public Law 119-21 reinstated the 100% special depreciation allowance for qualified property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025 (Instructions for Form 4562, 2025).

question: A business acquired a machine in December 2024 and placed it in service in March 2025. Its special depreciation allowance is limited to:
explanation: Property acquired before January 20, 2025 and placed in service in 2025 keeps the phase-down rate of 40% (Instructions for Form 4562, 2025). Only property acquired after January 19, 2025 gets 100%.

question: A business that does not want the special depreciation allowance may elect out of it:
optionB: For all assets in all years
optionC: For a whole class of property
explanation: Section 168(k)(7) lets a taxpayer elect out for any class of property, applying to all property in that class placed in service that year, by a statement with the timely filed return.

question: Used equipment bought in 2025 from an unrelated dealer, never before used by the buyer, is:
optionC: Eligible only after 2 years of use
explanation: Since 2017 section 168(k)(2)(E)(ii) allows bonus depreciation on used property if the taxpayer did not use it before and did not acquire it from a related party.

question: For tax years beginning after 2024, domestic research or experimental expenditures may be:
explanation: New section 174A, from Public Law 119-21, allows a current deduction for domestic research or experimental expenditures, or an election to amortize them over at least 60 months. Foreign research stays on a 15-year schedule.

question: Under MACRS GDS, a computer used in a business is:
explanation: Section 168(e)(3)(B) lists computers and peripheral equipment, along with cars and light trucks, as 5-year property. Office furniture is 7-year property.

question: Qualified improvement property, an interior improvement to a nonresidential building, placed in service in 2025 has a GDS recovery period of:
explanation: Section 168(e)(3)(E)(vii) makes qualified improvement property 15-year property, so it also qualifies for bonus depreciation. Improvements that enlarge the building, or to elevators or the internal structural framework, are excluded.

question: Which business asset cannot be depreciated?
explanation: Land has no determinable useful life, so it is never depreciated. Land improvements such as paving and fences are 15-year property, and a rental house is 27.5-year property.

question: Depreciation on a new machine begins when it is:
explanation: Property is placed in service when it is ready and available for a specifically assigned function, even if not yet used. Payment and ordering do not start depreciation.

question: For section 1231, depreciable business equipment must have been held:
explanation: Section 1231(b) covers depreciable property and real property used in a trade or business and held for more than one year. Equipment held a year or less produces ordinary gain or loss.

question: A business has a 2025 net section 1231 gain and no net 1231 losses in prior years. The gain is treated as:
explanation: When section 1231 gains exceed 1231 losses and there are no nonrecaptured losses from the prior 5 years, the net gain is long-term capital gain. A net 1231 loss would instead be ordinary.

question: A 2025 net section 1231 gain is treated as ordinary to the extent of net section 1231 losses deducted in the prior:
explanation: Section 1231(c) recaptures nonrecaptured net 1231 losses from the 5 most recent preceding years by treating that much of the current net gain as ordinary income.

question: Business use of a car on which accelerated depreciation was claimed falls to 45% in 2025. The owner must:
explanation: Section 280F(b)(2) recaptures the excess of depreciation claimed over what straight-line ADS would have allowed once qualified business use drops to 50% or less, and ADS applies from then on.

question: A business without an applicable financial statement may elect to deduct property costing up to what amount under the de minimis safe harbor?
explanation: Notice 2015-82 raised the de minimis safe harbor to $2,500 per invoice or item for taxpayers without an applicable financial statement. Those with one may use $5,000.

question: Building maintenance qualifies for the routine maintenance safe harbor if the owner expects to do it:
explanation: Reg. 1.263(a)-3(i) treats recurring work as routine for a building only if the taxpayer reasonably expects to perform it more than once in the 10 years after the building or system is placed in service.

question: The safe harbor for small taxpayers lets qualifying owners deduct building repairs if the building's unadjusted basis is:
explanation: Under Reg. 1.263(a)-3(h), a taxpayer with average gross receipts of $10 million or less may deduct work on a building with unadjusted basis of $1,000,000 or less if total costs do not exceed the lesser of $10,000 or 2% of that basis.

question: Unlike cost depletion, percentage depletion on a qualifying mineral property:
explanation: Percentage depletion under section 613 is a set percentage of gross income from the property and can continue after basis is recovered. Timber may use only cost depletion.

question: A business claimed no depreciation on a rental building for three years. To recover the missed amounts it generally:
optionB: Files Form 3115 for a method change
optionC: Claims all of it on this return
optionD: Can no longer recover any of it
explanation: Using an impermissible method for two or more years is a method of accounting, so the fix is an automatic change on Form 3115 with a section 481(a) adjustment for the missed depreciation.

question: When a business fails to claim depreciation, the asset's basis is still reduced by:
explanation: Section 1016(a)(2) reduces basis by the greater of depreciation allowed or allowable, so skipping a deduction does not preserve basis for a later sale.

question: Business equipment is destroyed in 2025, and the insurance paid exceeds its basis. To defer the gain, a replacement must generally be bought by:
explanation: Section 1033(a)(2)(B) allows replacement until 2 years after the close of the first tax year in which any gain is realized, so 2025 gain allows until the end of 2027. The 3-year period is for condemned business or investment real property.

question: Goodwill acquired as part of buying a business in 2025 is:
explanation: Section 197 amortizes acquired goodwill, going-concern value and other section 197 intangibles ratably over 15 years from the month of acquisition. Self-created goodwill is not amortizable.

question: A business swaps one rental building for another in a like-kind exchange with no gain recognized. It reports the exchange on:
explanation: Publication 544 says to report a like-kind exchange on Form 8824 even when no gain or loss is recognized. Any recognized gain then flows to Form 4797 or Schedule D.

question: An owner stops using a business truck for business and keeps it for personal driving. Depreciation:
explanation: Depreciation is allowed only while property is used in a business or held for income. Converting it to personal use is not a sale, so section 1245 recapture waits until a later disposition, apart from any section 179 or listed-property recapture.

question: An electing real property trade or business that opts out of the business interest limit must depreciate its buildings using:
explanation: Section 168(g)(1)(F) requires ADS for nonresidential real property, residential rental property and qualified improvement property held by an electing real property trade or business, which also bars bonus depreciation on them.

question: Schedule M-1 of Form 1120 reconciles:
optionB: Retained earnings from year to year
explanation: Schedule M-1 starts from net income per books and lists the items that differ for tax to reach taxable income. Schedule M-2 analyzes retained earnings, and Schedule L is the balance sheet.

question: On Schedule M-1, federal income tax expense recorded on the books is:
explanation: Federal income tax is not deductible, so the book expense is added back to book income to move toward taxable income.

question: On Schedule M-1, tax-exempt interest included in book income is:
explanation: Tax-exempt interest is income on the books but not taxable, so it appears among the items recorded on the books but not included on the return and is subtracted.

question: A corporation's ending retained earnings on Schedule L should agree with:
optionA: The last line of Schedule M-1
optionD: The ending balance on Schedule M-2
explanation: Schedule M-2 analyzes unappropriated retained earnings per books from the beginning to the end of the year, so its ending balance should match retained earnings on the year-end balance sheet.

question: Under the accrual method, an expense is deductible once all events fix the liability, the amount is reasonably determinable, and:
optionB: The bill has been paid in full
explanation: Section 461(h) adds the economic performance requirement: generally, services or property must be provided, or for some liabilities payment made, before the deduction is allowed.

question: A C corporation may use the cash method for 2025 if it:
optionC: Is owned by five or fewer people
explanation: Section 448 bars C corporations from the cash method unless they meet the section 448(c) average gross receipts test or are qualified personal service corporations or farming businesses.

question: A business switching from the cash method to the accrual method generally needs to file:
explanation: A change in overall accounting method needs IRS consent, requested on Form 3115, often under the automatic procedures. Form 1128 is for changing the tax year.

question: A method change produces a positive section 481(a) adjustment. It is generally taken into income over:
explanation: The Form 3115 instructions spread a positive adjustment over the year of change and the next 3 years. A negative adjustment is generally taken all in the year of change.

question: A business that uses a hybrid method commonly uses:
explanation: A business that must account for inventories may use the accrual method for purchases and sales and the cash method for other items, as long as the combination clearly reflects income.

question: A partner's share of the partnership's nondeductible expenses:
explanation: Section 705(a)(2)(B) decreases a partner's basis by the share of expenditures that are not deductible and not capital, such as the disallowed half of meals and penalties.

question: For the section 267 loss rules, which person is not a member of Ed's family?
explanation: Section 267(c)(4) counts only brothers and sisters (whole or half blood), a spouse, ancestors and lineal descendants as family. In-laws are not included, so a loss sale to a sister-in-law is not disallowed by that rule.

question: A corporation lends its sole shareholder $200,000 interest-free, payable on demand. The result is:
explanation: Section 7872 treats a below-market corporation-shareholder loan as if the corporation paid the forgone interest to the shareholder as a dividend and the shareholder paid it back as interest. Wages arise only in an employer-employee loan.

question: A corporation advances cash to its shareholder with no note, no interest and no repayment schedule. The advances are likely:
explanation: Without the marks of a real loan, such as a note, interest, a fixed schedule and actual repayment, the IRS may treat withdrawals as constructive dividends to the extent of earnings and profits.

question: A car dealer receives $6,000 in currency for a car and, three weeks later, $5,000 more in currency from the same buyer for that car. The dealer:
optionC: Files only if one payment tops $10,000
explanation: Related payments for one transaction are added together for Form 8300, so once the total exceeds $10,000 the dealer must file within 15 days of the payment that pushes it over.

question: A business generally need not issue Form 1099-NEC for $3,000 of services paid to:
optionD: An LLC taxed as a partnership
explanation: Payments to corporations are generally exempt from Form 1099-NEC reporting. Payments to attorneys are an exception and are reported even when the law firm is a corporation.

question: A contractor refuses to give a business a taxpayer identification number. The business must backup withhold at:
explanation: Section 3406 sets backup withholding at the fourth-lowest individual rate, 24% since 2018. The withholding is reported on Form 945.

question: An employer that reported $45,000 of Form 941 taxes in its lookback period deposits employment taxes:
explanation: Publication 15 makes an employer a monthly schedule depositor for the year if lookback-period taxes were $50,000 or less, and a semiweekly depositor above that.

question: A monthly depositor accumulates $105,000 of employment taxes on one day. The taxes must be deposited by:
explanation: Under the $100,000 next-day deposit rule, any employer that accumulates $100,000 or more of tax on any day must deposit by the next business day, and becomes a semiweekly depositor.

question: Under an accountable plan, expense reimbursements to employees are:
explanation: Reimbursements under an accountable plan are not wages and are not reported on Form W-2, as long as the employee substantiates expenses and returns any excess within a reasonable period.

question: To keep an allowance arrangement accountable, employees must substantiate expenses and also:
explanation: Publication 15 requires a business connection, substantiation within a reasonable period and return of amounts above substantiated expenses. Excess an employee keeps is wages.

question: Adequate records for business use of a car show, for each trip, the miles, the date, the destination and:
explanation: Section 274(d) and Publication 463 require records of the amount, time, place and business purpose of each use. Fuel receipts support actual expenses but do not prove business use.

question: Under common-law rules, a worker is most likely an employee when the business has the right to:
optionB: Control how the work is done
explanation: The common-law test looks at behavioral control, financial control and the relationship. The right to direct and control how the work is done is the key mark of employment, whatever a contract calls the worker.

question: Section 530 relief can protect a business that treated workers as contractors if it filed all required Forms 1099, had a reasonable basis, and:
explanation: Section 530 of the Revenue Act of 1978 requires reporting consistency, substantive consistency (no similar worker treated as an employee) and a reasonable basis. Withholding would show employee treatment.

question: For 2025 the employer shared responsibility rules apply to an employer that last year averaged at least:
explanation: Section 4980H applies to an applicable large employer, one with an average of at least 50 full-time employees, counting full-time equivalents, in the prior calendar year.

question: Under the Affordable Care Act employer rules, a full-time employee averages at least:
explanation: Section 4980H(c)(4) defines a full-time employee as one employed an average of at least 30 hours of service a week, or 130 hours a month.

question: A main tax drawback of a C corporation compared with an S corporation is that:
optionB: Its profits can be taxed twice
explanation: A C corporation pays tax on its income and shareholders pay tax again on dividends. An S corporation's income passes through once; the 100-shareholder limit applies to S corporations, not C corporations.

question: A shareholder pays personal bills from the corporate account without recording them. The main tax risk is:
explanation: Corporate payments of an owner's personal expenses are not business deductions and may be treated as constructive dividends, or wages if paid as compensation, to the owner.

question: The trust fund recovery penalty for unpaid withheld employment taxes may be assessed against:
explanation: Section 6672 makes any person responsible for collecting and paying over trust fund taxes who willfully fails to do so personally liable for 100% of the unpaid trust fund amount.

question: A complex trust's exemption on its 2025 Form 1041 is:
explanation: Section 642(b) gives an estate $600, a trust required to distribute all income currently $300, and any other trust, including a complex trust, $100.

question: A trust is a grantor trust when the grantor keeps:
explanation: Section 676 treats the grantor as owner when the grantor or a nonadverse party can revest the trust property in the grantor. A reversion makes a grantor trust under section 673 only if it exceeds 5% of value at inception.

question: Capital gains that the trust instrument allocates to corpus and that are not distributed are generally:
explanation: Section 643(a)(3) excludes gains allocated to corpus and not paid, credited or required to be distributed, so the trust itself pays tax on them.

question: A trust's deduction for distributions to beneficiaries is limited to its:
explanation: Sections 651 and 661 cap the distribution deduction at distributable net income, which also caps what beneficiaries must include.

question: Most trusts, other than tax-exempt and charitable trusts, must use:
explanation: Section 644 requires a trust's tax year to be the calendar year, except for tax-exempt and wholly charitable trusts. An estate may choose a fiscal year.

question: A section 645 election allows the executor and trustee to:
optionA: Split the estate into separate trusts
optionB: Fold a revocable trust into the estate
optionC: Skip Form 1041 for the first year
optionD: Treat the estate as a grantor trust
explanation: Section 645, made on Form 8855, treats a qualified revocable trust as part of the decedent's estate, so it can use the estate's fiscal year and other estate rules.

question: A calendar-year trust's 2025 Form 1041 and its Schedules K-1 are due by:
explanation: The Form 1041 instructions set the 15th day of the 4th month after year end, April 15, 2026, for calendar-year estates and trusts. Form 7004 gives a 5 1/2 month extension.

question: Tax-exempt interest a trust distributes to a beneficiary is, in the beneficiary's hands:
explanation: Under section 652(b) and 662(b), distributed amounts keep the character they had in the trust, in proportion to the items in DNI, so tax-exempt interest stays tax-exempt.

question: An arrangement moves a business into trusts while the owner keeps full control and use of the income. For tax purposes it is:
explanation: The Form 1041 instructions warn that abusive trust arrangements with no real change in control or benefit are disregarded, and the income is taxed to the person who controls it.

question: A simple trust earns $12,000 of interest, all of which it must distribute in 2025. Who reports the interest?
explanation: A simple trust deducts income required to be distributed, up to DNI, and the beneficiary includes it from Schedule K-1 whether or not it was actually paid.

question: Under the tier system, first-tier beneficiaries are those entitled to:
explanation: First-tier distributions are income required to be distributed currently and carry out DNI first. All other amounts paid or credited are second-tier distributions.

question: A complex trust may take a charitable deduction for an amount that is:
explanation: Section 642(c) allows an unlimited deduction for gross income paid for a charitable purpose under the governing instrument. The individual percentage limits of section 170 do not apply.

question: A new charity files Form 1023 for recognition retroactive to its formation. It must generally file within:
explanation: Publication 557 makes exemption effective from formation if Form 1023 is filed within 27 months from the end of the month the organization was organized.

question: An exempt organization may file Form 990-N instead of a full return if its gross receipts are normally:
explanation: The Form 990 instructions allow organizations with gross receipts normally $50,000 or less to submit the Form 990-N e-Postcard, unless they choose to file Form 990 or 990-EZ.

question: An organization may file Form 990-EZ if gross receipts are under $200,000 and year-end total assets are under:
explanation: The Form 990 instructions allow Form 990-EZ when gross receipts are less than $200,000 and total assets at year end are less than $500,000.

question: Form 990-PF is the annual return of:
explanation: Every private foundation files Form 990-PF regardless of its income. Public charities file Form 990, 990-EZ or 990-N, churches are not required to file, and political organizations file Form 990 or 1120-POL.

question: A calendar-year exempt organization's 2025 Form 990 is due on:
explanation: The Form 990 instructions set the 15th day of the 5th month after the year ends, May 15 for a calendar-year filer.

question: Which activity of a charity is excluded from unrelated business income?
optionA: A gift shop with paid staff
explanation: Section 513(a)(1) excludes a trade or business in which substantially all the work is done by unpaid volunteers. Advertising and debt-financed income are classic sources of UBTI.

question: An exempt organization must file Form 990-T if its gross unrelated business income is:
explanation: Publication 598 requires Form 990-T when gross income from all unrelated businesses is $1,000 or more. A specific deduction of $1,000 is allowed when figuring UBTI.

question: Rent an exempt organization receives from real property it owns free of debt is, for UBTI:
explanation: Section 512(b)(3) excludes rents from real property from UBTI, unless the property is debt-financed or the rent depends on the tenant's net income. Dividends, interest and royalties are excluded too.

question: An employer's SEP contribution for an employee may not exceed the smaller of an indexed dollar limit or what share of compensation?
explanation: Publication 560 caps SEP contributions at the smaller of 25% of the employee's compensation or the year's dollar limit. For a self-employed owner the 25% works out to 20% of net earnings.

question: For 2025, a self-employed person may set up and fund a SEP as late as:
explanation: Publication 560 allows a SEP to be set up for a year as late as the due date, including extensions, of the employer's return for that year, with contributions made by the same date.

question: A business that has never had a SIMPLE IRA plan wants one for 2025. It must generally set the plan up by:
explanation: Publication 560 says a new SIMPLE IRA plan may be set up any time between January 1 and October 1 of the year. A new employer that comes into existence after October 1 may set one up as soon as possible.

question: Under a SIMPLE IRA plan, an employer that matches elective deferrals must generally match dollar for dollar up to:
explanation: The SIMPLE IRA match is up to 3% of compensation, reducible to 1% in 2 of 5 years. The alternative is a 2% nonelective contribution for every eligible employee, not a 2% match.

question: A 45-year-old withdraws from a SIMPLE IRA 18 months after first joining the plan, and no exception applies. The additional tax is:
explanation: Section 72(t)(6) raises the 10% additional tax to 25% for SIMPLE IRA distributions within 2 years after the employee first participated, unless an exception applies.

question: A disqualified person engages in a prohibited transaction with a plan. The first-tier excise tax is:
explanation: Section 4975(a) imposes a 15% first-tier tax for each year in the taxable period. A 100% second-tier tax applies if the transaction is not corrected.

question: A one-participant 401(k) plan covering only the owner must file Form 5500-EZ when year-end plan assets are:
explanation: Publication 560 excuses a one-participant plan from Form 5500-EZ for a year when total assets were $250,000 or less, except for its final plan year.

question: An employer deducts compensation paid under a nonqualified deferred compensation plan:
optionB: When it funds a rabbi trust
explanation: Section 404(a)(5) delays the employer's deduction until the year the amount is includible in the employee's income, matching the deduction to the inclusion.

question: A cash-method farmer who usually sells a crop the year after harvest receives 2025 crop insurance proceeds for drought damage. The farmer may elect to:
explanation: Section 451(f) and Publication 225 let a cash-method farmer postpone crop insurance and disaster payments to the following year if under normal practice the crop would have been sold then.

question: Breeding cattle sold by a farmer qualify as section 1231 property if they were held:
explanation: Publication 225 treats livestock held for draft, breeding, dairy or sport as section 1231 property after 12 months, or 24 months for cattle and horses.

question: A farmer sells more livestock than usual because of drought in a designated area. The gain can be deferred if replacement livestock is bought within:
explanation: Section 1033(e)(2) extends the replacement period to 4 years for livestock sold on account of drought, flood or other weather conditions in an applicable region, and longer while the region stays drought-listed.

question: Form 4835 is used by:
optionA: A tenant farmer who works the land
optionD: A landowner who does not materially participate
explanation: Form 4835 reports crop or livestock shares received as rent by a landowner who did not materially participate in the farming. That income is not subject to self-employment tax and goes to Schedule E.

question: Schedule J (Form 1040) lets a farmer:
optionA: Average farm income over 3 prior years
optionC: Defer it over the next 3 years
optionD: Exclude part of it up to a cap
explanation: Farm income averaging taxes elected farm income at the rates of the 3 prior base years, which can lower the tax in a high-income year. It does not defer or exclude the income.

question: Cash patronage dividends a farmer receives from a cooperative based on purchases of deducted farm supplies are:
explanation: Publication 225 includes patronage dividends from purchases of business supplies in farm income, since the supplies were deducted. Dividends from personal purchases would instead reduce cost.

question: A building is residential rental property for MACRS only if dwelling units produce at least what share of its gross rents?
explanation: Section 168(e)(2)(A) and Publication 527 require 80% or more of gross rental income from dwelling units. A building that falls short is nonresidential real property with a 39-year life.

question: A homeowner rents her residence for 12 days in 2025 and lives in it the rest of the year. The rent is:
explanation: Section 280A(g) excludes rent when a dwelling used as a home is rented fewer than 15 days in the year, and no rental expenses are deducted.

question: A vacation home is treated as a residence if personal use exceeds the greater of:
explanation: Section 280A(d)(1) treats a dwelling as a residence when personal use is more than the greater of 14 days or 10% of the days it is rented at fair rent, and then limits rental deductions to rental income.

question: A landlord collects a refundable security deposit at signing. The deposit is:
explanation: Publication 527 excludes a security deposit the landlord plans to return. It becomes income only when kept, for example for damage or unpaid rent.

question: A tenant pays the last month's rent at signing in 2025 for a lease ending in 2027. The landlord reports it:
explanation: Publication 527 treats advance rent as income when received, whatever period it covers and whatever accounting method the landlord uses.

question: A real estate professional who owns six rentals must materially participate in each one unless she:
optionA: Owns fewer than ten rental units
optionB: Hires a property manager for all
optionD: Elects to group them as one activity
explanation: Section 469(c)(7)(A) applies rental by rental unless the taxpayer elects to treat all interests in rental real estate as a single activity, which makes material participation easier to meet.
